commentary_summary: The utilisation of Supramax vessels rose marginally WoW, reaching last year's level. | Meanwhile, the tonnemile index moderated last week but remained much higher compared to last year. | The Supramax employability increased as the YTD coal exports from Indonesia expanded. Substantial expansion in imports from India, where the government has urged power producers to import 6% of total coal requirements for blending, has contributed to the vessel demand. | The laden tonnage at anchor in the Indian ports has reached the highest levels in 2024, with approximately 5.2 mdwt waiting to unload.

Drewry's tonnemile index for Supramax vessels remained on an uptrend for the third consecutive week, with a 10.7% rise YoY. | This is juxtaposed with the lowest inactivity levels in the Supramax segment after 2021, resulting in ample supply in the market, keeping utilisation levels subdued. | The tonnage underway in the West has reached historically high, with 40 mdwt underway. | Meanwhile, ample coal demand in Asia has also kept the share of laden vessels in the East high. As a result, the spot rates on the Indonesia-China route have been rising.

The tonnemile index moderated WoW, reaching 98.7 last week from 100.1 the week before. While the share of laden vessels moderated in the East, it continued to be on an uptrend in the West. The share continues to be much higher compared to the last year in both regions. | The significant rise of 1.3 mdwt laden tonnage at anchor in India indicates a surge in import activity due to buoyant demand for coal from Indonesia. | Meanwhile, the Atlantic, particularly the US Gulf, experienced lower tonnage availability due to increased demand for wood pellets from the US Gulf to Japan and grains from the US Gulf to North Coast South America.

The laden tonne-mile index increased by 2.1% WoW, primarily driven by steady demand for tonnage in the ECSA and the USG. Soybean exports from the US have expanded rapidly ahead of the election results due to the fear of tariffs. Since more than 20% of the shipments to China are on Supramax vessels, the demand has risen over the last week and is likely to sustain in the short term. | Increased demand resulted in a surge in congestion in the Atlantic, leading to higher ballast tonnage waiting at load ports. | Meanwhile, congestion in China has increased over the week driven by increased shipments of soybean as well as coal.

commentary_title: Aggravated seasonal lull in Supramax demand
commentary_summary: The utilisation for Supramax vessels declined marginally WoW but remain substantially lower than last year due to the aggravated seasonal lull in market activity. | The ballast speed continued to be on a downtrend in response to subdued fixtures, dampening the supply utilisation. Correspondingly, the tonnemile index remained weak, ending at 87.1 points last week, down from 92.2 in week 1. | As the market is engulfed with bleak activity due to the Lunar New Year Holidays in China, the congestion at major Chinese ports is subdued. Additionally, China secured most of its soybean stocks for 1Q25 ahead of Trump assuming the office in January 2025, which has aggravated the seasonal lull in the recent weeks.

commentary_title: Weakness prevails in the Supramax market
commentary_summary: The Supramax tonne-miles index weakened slightly in week 16, down by 0.4, as market tonnage demand remained soft. This was in tandem with falling utilisation, ending the week at 93.2%. | Ballast speed in the west dropped to its lowest levels since 2022. There was also a sharp decline in the percentage of laden vessels in the west. In accordance, Spot rates on the USG-Europe route fell by 4.6%. | Vessels at anchor in the East increased by 17% MoM, leading to higher congestion of both laden and ballast vessels at anchor. Laden tonnage at anchor in the Pacific increased sharply by 36% WoW due to early May orders from the west, mainly for salt and grains.

commentary_title: Supramax markets faces diverging regional trends
commentary_summary: Supramax utilisation posted a modest gain of 0.6 percentage points over the past week, reflecting a market split between regions. | The Atlantic basin gained momentum, with the US Gulf standing out as the key driver of positive sentiment. Supporting this trend, the number of vessels in port in the West rose by nearly 4% MoM. | In contrast, the Pacific market continued to face headwinds from vessel oversupply, leading to reduced congestion among ballasting ships. | Vessel speed trends were mixed, although global ballast speeds trended higher overall.

Supramax utilisation rose 0.7 percentage points WoW in week 38, with ballast speeds and Baltic benchmark rates also edging higher. | The loading and discharge activity at port in the West rose 11.5% MoM in September while it improved 5.5% in the East. Spot rates also imporved in the West on US-Europe route further implying the improved market sentiments. | While the ballast congestion in China remained low this week, it saw an sharp increase in Oceania. Laden tonnage in Atlantic also remanied high, constantly above than 2024 levels.

commentary_title: Atlantic leads gains in supramax sector
commentary_summary: Supramax utilisation rose 1.4% in week 45 to 93.5%, supported by a continued uptrend in tonne-mile demand in 2H25 and a MoM increase in vessel capacity at port in the East. | At the same time, capacity at anchor has been declining, thereby easing congestion. Baltic benchmarks tracked the higher utilisation, with spot rates holding firm across both East and West. | In the Atlantic, sentiment remained positive, with tight vessel availability and stronger enquiry from the US Gulf, following China’s commitment to purchase 12 million tonnes of US soybeans this season and 25 million tonnes annually over the next three years.

commentary_title: Atlantic resilience offsets Holiday-driven weakness in Asia
commentary_summary: The Supramax market softened during the week, with the Baltic benchmark S10TC declining to $19,050/day alongside falling vessel Utilisation. Trading activity slowed considerably due to May Day holidays and the Geneva dry bulk events, while enquiries in the Pacific also dwindled. Indonesian coal activity remained subdued, and high Chinese coal inventories continued to cap demand, resulting in weaker sentiment across Asian routes. | The Atlantic continued to outperform the Pacific, supported by firm demand from the Continent and Mediterranean for ECSA and the US Gulf. Although the US Gulf came under pressure from an increase in ballasting vessels and fewer fresh cargoes, the Mediterranean, Black Sea and West Africa remained relatively firm. | While sentiment remained mixed, specific regional trades continued to underpin the market. Strong Pakistani coal demand lifted South Africa's exports, and the Indian Ocean market improved modestly. Meanwhile, firm steel demand supported Far East–West Africa fixtures, and expectations of higher demand for ECSA and US Gulf cargoes helped maintain positive sentiment in the Atlantic.

commentary_title: Summer slowdown weighs on Atlantic while Asia remains supported
commentary_summary: The Supramax tonne-miles index edged down 3% to reach 117.7 in week 30, as the summer holiday season reduced new cargo enquiries across most regions. Softer spot rates reflected limited early-to-mid-August cargoes, particularly in the US Gulf, where greater vessel availability forced owners to compete for vessel employment. | The US Gulf faced the sharpest correction as a lack of new cargoes and a growing list of vessels weighed on fronthaul and transatlantic rates. The Continent also softened amid weaker Turkish scrap and fertiliser demand, while the East Mediterranean remained comparatively resilient, supported by new grain cargoes and stronger premiums for owners willing to trade via the Red Sea. | The Pacific lost some momentum as enquiries from North Asia eased and vessel availability increased across Southeast Asia and East Coast India. However, steady Chinese demand for Indonesian coal, continued South African cargoes in the Indian Ocean, and improving Australian export activity helped limit further downside.

commentary_title: Asian strength leads steady gains amid tightening tonnage in Supramax market
commentary_summary: The Supramax vessel utilisation increased WoW to 93.7% in tandem with rising tonne-miles index and Baltic benchmark rates to $20,300, with firm NoPac grain and backhaul demand supporting the Far East. Indonesian coal remained a key driver, with Indonesia-India, while South Africa-India/Pakistan business reached as also reached new highs. | US Gulf fronthaul and transatlantic demand improved, with Ultramaxes achieving rates in the $30,000s/day range. The Continent saw strong activity as fertiliser and grain absorbed available tonnage, while expanded Black Sea requirements further tightened vessel availability and pushed scrap rates higher. | Strong fixing activity across both basins, combined with fewer available vessels and firm backhaul demand, has encouraged owners to hold for higher rates. Period activity has consequently picked up, while the FFA remains supportive heading into Q4.
